title: When the Hollow Sings Anew
premise: Ansel Quintana has spent her life hiding the beast-speaker gift that once got her mother burned, guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while pretending to be merely a good tracker. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes in a single night, she discovers her long-lost brother's soul was sold to the Hollow Court beneath the mountain — and that the usurper Veyra Marchen intends to feed the free cities' souls to the starving court to fuel her armies. Ansel must ally with a disgraced ward-keeper, a traitorous courtier, and the beasts she was taught to fear, trading pieces of her own memory as payment for passage deeper into the Hollow. In the end she wins back her brother's soul but must choose between destroying the court (and the mountain cities it anchors) or binding herself to it as its new voice; she chooses binding, sacrificing her freedom so the stars can return, and walks out of the Thornfell half-hollow, singing.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons in the northern ranges before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about borders — between nations, species, and the selves we trade away to survive.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel guides a smuggler caravan through Thornfell, quietly bargaining with a mountain lion for safe passage — a glimpse of her forbidden gift. POV: Ansel. Beat: competence and concealment; she is good at her life but never at home in it.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Scars
chapters.summary: At the border town of Cinderhatch, Ansel notices the ancient wards humming wrong, like a struck bell fading. A drunk ward-keeper, Odile Ferran, rants that something beneath the mountain is drinking them dry. POV: Ansel. Beat: unease; the world's foundations are cracking.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every star goes out at once. The wards fall with a sound like breaking glass heard underground. Panicked refugees flood Cinderhatch; Ansel's beasts flee downslope, screaming warnings only she can hear. POV: Ansel. Beat: terror and awe.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Carried Back
chapters.summary: A dying wolf reaches Ansel carrying a scrap of cloth bearing her family crest — from the Hollow Court beneath the mountain. Inside its folds, a name: her brother Tomas, sold twenty years ago. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief reopened; a personal stake ignites.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Herald
chapters.summary: Veyra Marchen's herald arrives in Cinderhatch offering 'protection' — conscription disguised as salvation. Ansel watches neighbors kneel and understands the free cities are already losing. POV: Ansel. Beat: dread; the political noose tightens.

chapters.title: Odile's Broken Compass
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the wards were anchored by souls pledged to the Hollow Court generations ago — including one pledge signed by Ansel's mother. She knows a way under the mountain. POV: Odile. Beat: reluctant alliance; guilt over the wards' fall.

chapters.title: Beasts at the Border
chapters.summary: Marchen's soldiers hunt 'gifted' refugees. Ansel uses her gift openly for the first time, turning a bear against a patrol, and realizes there is no going back to hiding. POV: Ansel. Beat: first open rebellion; exhilaration shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Ansel's old smuggling network offers passage beneath the mountain — in exchange for her leading Marchen's forces through Thornfell instead. Loyalty vs. survival splits her oldest friendships. POV: Ansel. Beat: betrayal offered; moral cost made concrete.

chapters.title: Down the Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: Ansel and Odile enter the Hollow through a flooded mine shaft, guided by blind cave bats whose song maps the dark. The court's hunger presses on them like deep water. POV: Ansel. Beat: threshold crossed; claustrophobic wonder.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: They reach the Hollow Court: a cathedral of bone and lantern-light where sold souls burn as currency. Ansel sees Tomas's soul-flame among thousands. POV: Ansel. Beat: horror and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Courtier of Ash
chapters.summary: A courtier named Sef Andrade — once human, now half-hollow — catches them. Instead of raising alarm, he offers help: he remembers being sold too, and hates what the court has become. POV: Sef. Beat: wary alliance; the enemy within.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Sef shows them the Ledger where every sale is written. Tomas's entry bears Marchen's family seal — the usurper's rise began with soul-debt. POV: Sef. Beat: revelation; personal grief becomes political weapon.

chapters.title: Memory as Coin
chapters.summary: To move freely in the court, Ansel pays tolls in memories — her mother's face, first. Each payment hollows her slightly; Sef warns the court always overcharges. POV: Ansel. Beat: sacrifice begins; the theme's price made literal.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Starves
chapters.summary: They glimpse the Hollow Queen: vast, patient, starving since the star-pact broke. She does not rage — she waits, and waiting is worse. POV: Odile. Beat: scale of threat established; dread deepens.

chapters.title: Above: The First City Falls
chapters.summary: Interlude above ground. Marchen's army takes Rivermoor without a battle; the city simply opens its gates. Refugees bring word down the smuggler roads. POV: Odile. Beat: ticking clock accelerates; despair.

chapters.title: Tomas, Almost
chapters.summary: Ansel reaches her brother's soul-flame. It recognizes her voice but cannot remember why — souls in the Ledger lose their names. She sings the lullaby their mother taught her. POV: Ansel. Beat: devastating tenderness; stakes become intimate.

chapters.title: The Courtier's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sef reveals stealing a soul from the Ledger requires a replacement of equal weight. He volunteers himself — he has little left to lose. Ansel refuses to let anyone pay for her family twice. POV: Sef. Beat: loyalty tested; self-sacrifice refused.

chapters.title: Hollowed Friends
chapters.summary: Odile is caught paying her own memories to learn the ward-restoring rite, and comes back not knowing Ansel's name. The cost of the quest starts consuming the questers. POV: Odile. Beat: tragedy among allies; corruption of purpose.

chapters.title: The Beasts Descend
chapters.summary: Ansel calls to the beasts of Thornfell through stone and root. They answer — wolves, bears, the blind bats — because the court's hunger threatens them too. Her forbidden gift becomes an army. POV: Ansel. Beat: empowerment; the hidden gift becomes the hope.

chapters.title: Marchen Below
chapters.summary: Veyra Marchen herself descends with her army, intending to offer the free cities' conscripted souls to the Queen in exchange for dominion. She and Ansel meet across the Ledger. POV: Marchen. Beat: antagonist revealed in full; chilling pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Devil's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marchen offers Ansel a deal: Tomas's soul freely given, in exchange for the beasts and the smuggler roads. Survival dressed as mercy. Ansel asks for a night to decide. POV: Ansel. Beat: temptation at its strongest.

chapters.title: What Mother Actually Did
chapters.summary: Reading the Ledger's older pages, Ansel learns her mother wasn't burned for beast-speaking — she burned herself willingly to seal a crack in the star-pact. The family legacy is sacrifice, not shame. POV: Ansel. Beat: reframing; inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ansel rejects Marchen's deal and triggers the beasts' assault on the court's outer galleries. Battle erupts in the dark; Sef turns on his fellow courtiers. POV: Sef. Beat: point of no return; war in the underworld.

chapters.title: The Queen Wakes
chapters.summary: The battle's noise wakes the Hollow Queen fully. She speaks into every mind at once, offering each combatant their deepest want. Half of Marchen's army defects to her on the spot. POV: Odile. Beat: climax pressure; desire as weapon.

chapters.title: Ledger Fire
chapters.summary: Odile, remembering fragments of her ward-keeper oaths, attempts to burn the Ledger and sever all soul-debts at once. The fire spreads through the court like dawn. POV: Odile. Beat: bold gambit; hope flaring.

chapters.title: The Cost of Burning
chapters.summary: Burning the Ledger unbinds the souls — but also unbinds the mountain itself, which the court's pact holds up. Cities above begin to tremble. Destroying the court may kill everyone it anchors. POV: Ansel. Beat: catastrophic twist; victory curdles.

chapters.title: Sef's Choice
chapters.summary: Sef, who knows the court's architecture from inside, leads civilians toward the exits while the mountain groans. He stays behind to hold a collapsing gallery, finally choosing his own name over survival. POV: Sef. Beat: noble death; loyalty fulfilled.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Root
chapters.summary: Ansel corners Marchen at the mountain's root, where the original star-pact was signed. Their duel is fought with words and debts as much as blades. POV: Ansel. Beat: antagonist defeated — but the larger problem remains.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: With Marchen dead and the Ledger ash, the court needs a voice to renegotiate the pact — someone who can speak to both beasts and hollow things. Every eye, hollow and human, turns to Ansel. POV: Ansel. Beat: the trap of power; the crown nobody wants.

chapters.title: The Queen's Question
chapters.summary: The Hollow Queen asks Ansel directly: destroy us and bury two cities, or bind yourself to us and hold the pact anew. There is no third door — or so the Queen believes. POV: Ansel. Beat: the thematic crucible; price of survival made ultimate.

chapters.title: Tomas Remembers
chapters.summary: Freed from the Ledger, Tomas's soul regains his name and memories. He begs her not to pay for him again. For one night, they are siblings in the dark, singing old songs. POV: Tomas. Beat: grace note before the decision; love without debt.

chapters.title: The Binding Rite
chapters.summary: Ansel agrees to bind — but on her terms: the court will feed on memory freely given, never stolen, and the beasts will be its wardens alongside the ward-keepers. The Queen, starving for trust more than souls, accepts. POV: Ansel. Beat: climax resolution; power accepted and immediately constrained.

chapters.title: Stars Return
chapters.summary: The pact renewed, the stars reignite over Thornfell one by one. Above, the trembling cities steady. Refugees look up and weep at lights they'd forgotten. POV: Odile. Beat: catharsis; the world exhales.

chapters.title: Half-Hollow
chapters.summary: Ansel climbs out of the mountain changed: part of her memory lives in the court now, and she hears its song always. She can leave, but never be entirely away. POV: Ansel. Beat: bittersweet transformation; survival's permanent mark.

chapters.title: Reckonings in Cinderhatch
chapters.summary: Back in Cinderhatch, the free cities debate what to do with Marchen's surrendered army and the truth of the soul-ledgers. Ansel testifies, naming names, including friends who nearly sold her. POV: Odile. Beat: justice and mercy weighed; loyalty vs. truth resolved publicly.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's New Road
chapters.summary: Ansel reopens the Thornfell roads — openly now, as a licensed guide and the court's ambassador. Her old network must decide whether to follow her into daylight. Some do; some don't. POV: Ansel. Beat: reconciliation incomplete; new order taking shape.

chapters.title: Letters to the Hollow
chapters.summary: People begin leaving memories at the court's gates voluntarily — griefs they want set down, joys they want kept forever. The court's economy transforms from theft to gift. POV: Sef's successor, a young courtier. Beat: healing systems; hope institutionalized.

chapters.title: The Song Anew
chapters.summary: On the anniversary of the starless night, Ansel stands on Thornfell's peak and sings the pact-song with the beasts, the court, and the cities below answering in turn. Tomas, restored to flesh by the freed souls' gratitude, harmonizes. POV: Ansel. Beat: full-circle joy; the title earned.

chapters.title: What Ansel Paid
chapters.summary: Quiet epilogue: Ansel visits her mother's memorial and finally understands the shape of her inheritance. She lists what she lost — faces, years, a nameless afternoon — and decides it was worth it, mostly. POV: Ansel. Beat: honest accounting; the price acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Sings
chapters.summary: Final chapter: travelers on the mountain roads sometimes hear singing from the stones and pause, unsure if it's wind. It isn't. The last image is Ansel walking the high passes at dusk, half here, half below, wholly herself. POV: Ansel. Beat: resonant close; mystery and peace held together.
